title: Hobbies & Daily Routine (爱好与日常生活)
description: Talk about your free time and your day in Mandarin: hobbies like 游泳 and 听音乐, daily routine verbs like 起床 and 做作业, frequency words like 每天 and 有时候, transport, and answering the phone with 喂.

notes.heading: 📌 Hobbies and Activities (爱好)
notes.body:
Hobbies are 爱好 (àihào). Many activity words are verb + object pairs:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 看书 | kànshū | to read (books) |
| 听音乐 | tīng yīnyuè | to listen to music |
| 打球 | dǎ qiú | to play ball |
| 游泳 | yóuyǒng | to swim |
| 画画 | huàhuà | to draw / paint |
| 唱歌 | chànggē | to sing |
| 跳舞 | tiàowǔ | to dance |
| 看电影 | kàn diànyǐng | to watch a film |

To say you like doing something, put 喜欢 (xǐhuan, to like) before the verb: 我喜欢游泳。 (Wǒ xǐhuan yóuyǒng.) — I like swimming.

To ask about someone else's hobbies: 你的爱好是什么? (Nǐ de àihào shì shénme?) — What is your hobby?

notes.heading: 🔑 Verb-Object Words Like 游泳
notes.body:
Many Chinese activity words are really a verb plus its object glued together: 游泳 = 游 (to swim) + 泳 (swim); 唱歌 = 唱 (to sing) + 歌 (song); 打球 = 打 (to hit/play) + 球 (ball).

Why it matters: to say HOW LONG or add extra information, you repeat the verb rather than splitting the pair in the middle.

- 我喜欢唱歌。 (Wǒ xǐhuan chànggē.) — I like singing.
- 她每天游泳。 (Tā měitiān yóuyǒng.) — She swims every day.

⚠️ Common mistake: do not treat 游泳 as one inseparable block with another verb after it. Say 我会游泳 (I can swim), not 我会去泳.

notes.heading: 📌 Daily Routine Verbs (日常生活)
notes.body:
These verbs describe a normal day from morning to night:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 起床 | qǐchuáng | to get up |
| 洗澡 | xǐzǎo | to take a shower / bath |
| 吃饭 | chīfàn | to eat (a meal) |
| 上学 | shàngxué | to go to school |
| 放学 | fàngxué | school finishes |
| 做作业 | zuò zuòyè | to do homework |
| 睡觉 | shuìjiào | to sleep / go to bed |

A whole day: 我七点起床，八点上学。下午四点放学，晚上我做作业，十点睡觉。 — I get up at seven and go to school at eight. School finishes at four in the afternoon; in the evening I do homework and go to sleep at ten.

notes.heading: 🔑 Frequency Words: 每天, 有时候, 常常
notes.body:
Say how often you do things with these frequency words:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 每天 | měitiān | every day |
| 常常 | chángcháng | often |
| 有时候 | yǒushíhou | sometimes |
| 总是 | zǒngshì | always |

🔑 How it works: time and frequency words go BEFORE the verb (and 每天 can go before or after the subject).

- 我每天做作业。 (Wǒ měitiān zuò zuòyè.) — I do homework every day.
- 我有时候走路去学校。 (Wǒ yǒushíhou zǒulù qù xuéxiào.) — I sometimes walk to school.
- 她常常唱歌。 (Tā chángcháng chànggē.) — She often sings.

⚠️ Common mistake: putting the time word after the verb like in English ("I get up at seven"). In Chinese, 七点 must come before 起床: 我七点起床。

notes.heading: 📌 Getting Around: Transport (交通)
notes.body:
How do you get to school? Learn these transport phrases:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 坐公共汽车 | zuò gōnggòng qìchē | to take the bus |
| 坐地铁 | zuò dìtiě | to take the underground / metro |
| 骑自行车 | qí zìxíngchē | to ride a bicycle |
| 走路 | zǒulù | to walk |
| 开车 | kāichē | to drive a car |

Use 坐 (zuò, to sit) for transport you ride in, and 骑 (qí, to ride astride) for bikes and horses.

To ask how someone travels: 你怎么去学校? (Nǐ zěnme qù xuéxiào?) — How do you get to school?

Answer: 我骑自行车上学。 (Wǒ qí zìxíngchē shàngxué.) — I go to school by bike.

notes.heading: 🔑 Word Order with Time
notes.body:
🔑 How it works: in Chinese, the time comes BEFORE the verb — the opposite of English.

English: I get up at seven every day.
Chinese: 我每天七点起床。 (Wǒ měitiān qī diǎn qǐchuáng.) — Literally: I every-day seven-o'clock get-up.

More examples:

- 我们早上八点半上课。 (Wǒmen zǎoshang bā diǎn bàn shàngkè.) — We start class at 8:30 in the morning.
- 他晚上十点睡觉。 (Tā wǎnshang shí diǎn shuìjiào.) — He goes to bed at ten at night.

Order inside the time phrase: bigger unit first — 早上 (morning) before 八点半 (8:30).

notes.heading: 💡 Making Phone Calls (打电话)
notes.body:
打电话 (dǎ diànhuà) means to make a phone call. Phone Chinese has its own special phrases:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 喂 | wéi | hello (only on the phone!) |
| 请问 | qǐngwèn | may I ask... (polite) |
| 等一下 | děng yíxià | wait a moment |
| 再见 | zàijiàn | goodbye |

A model call:

A: 喂，你好! (Wéi, nǐ hǎo!) — Hello!
B: 喂，请问，小明在家吗? (Wéi, qǐngwèn, Xiǎo Míng zài jiā ma?) — Hello, may I ask, is Xiao Ming at home?
A: 在。你等一下。 (Zài. Nǐ děng yíxià.) — Yes, he is. Wait a moment.
B: 谢谢! (Xièxie!) — Thanks!

⚠️ Common mistake: 喂 (wéi, 2nd/4th tone) is only for answering the phone — in person you greet people with 你好 (nǐ hǎo), not 喂.

✅ Check: can you answer the phone, ask for someone politely, and say goodbye?

questions.explanation: 游泳 (yóuyǒng) means to swim. It is a verb-object word: 游 is the verb "to swim" and 泳 is its object.
起床 (qǐchuáng) means to get up — 起 is rise and 床 is bed, literally "rise from bed". Going to bed is 睡觉 (shuìjiào).

questions.stem: 我喜欢听音乐。 What does this sentence mean?
choices: I listen to music every day.
questions.explanation: 听 (tīng) means to listen and 音乐 (yīnyuè) is music, so 我喜欢听音乐 means I like listening to music.
每 (měi) means every, so 每天 (měitiān) is every day. 明天 is tomorrow and 昨天 is yesterday.
做 (zuò) means to do and 作业 (zuòyè) is homework, so 做作业 means to do homework.

questions.stem: 我有时候走路去学校。 What does this sentence mean?
choices: I walk to school every day.
questions.explanation: 有时候 (yǒushíhou) means sometimes and it goes before the verb phrase 走路去学校 (walk to school): I sometimes walk to school.

questions.stem: Which sentence has the correct Chinese word order for "I get up at seven every day"?
questions.explanation: In Chinese, time words come before the verb, bigger unit first: 每天 (every day) then 七点 (seven o'clock), then 起床 (get up).

questions.stem: 坐公共汽车 (zuò gōnggòng qìchē) means:
questions.explanation: 坐 (zuò) means to sit/ride and 公共汽车 is a public bus, so 坐公共汽车 means to take the bus.
睡觉 (shuìjiào) means to sleep or to go to bed, as in 我十点睡觉 — I go to bed at ten.

questions.stem: 你怎么去学校? What is this question asking?
choices: When do you go to school?
How do you get to school?
questions.explanation: 怎么 (zěnme) asks how, so 你怎么去学校 asks how you get to school — the answer would be a transport phrase like 我骑自行车上学.

questions.stem: You answer a phone call in Chinese. What do you say first?
questions.explanation: 喂 (wéi) is the special word for answering the phone, followed by 你好. 再见 is goodbye, used at the end of the call.

questions.stem: 我常常和朋友打球。 What does this sentence mean?
choices: I often play ball with my friends.
I like playing ball with my friends.
I played ball with my friends yesterday.
questions.explanation: 常常 (chángcháng) means often and 和 (hé) means with: I often play ball with my friends.
骑 (qí) is to ride astride and 自行车 (zìxíngchē) is a bicycle, so 骑自行车 means to ride a bike.

choices: school finishes / to be let out of school
questions.explanation: 放 (fàng) means to release, so 放学 (fàngxué) is when school finishes for the day. Going to school is 上学 (shàngxué).

questions.stem: 喂，请问，张明在家吗? Where would you hear this, and what does it mean?
choices: On the phone — is Zhang Ming at home?
In a shop — how much does this cost?
At school — is Zhang Ming in class today?
At a restaurant — can I order some food?
questions.explanation: 喂 (wéi) signals a phone call, and 请问 ... 在家吗 politely asks whether Zhang Ming is at home.
